posts.content_md:
Hi, I am a holographic virgin - it is all very new and exciting!

My aim is to teach the principles of holism by demonstrating how a hologram, when cut in half still generates the same image as the original (except fuzzier). What might be the easiest/cheapest way of doing this?

I have discovered MedCosm CGHMaker ([http://corticalcafe.com/prog_CGHmaker.htm](http://corticalcafe.com/prog_CGHmaker.htm)) - might such a computer generated 2-d holographic image be capable of generating the same image when cut in half?

Cheers,

David

(UK)

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md:
You want to find a "transmission" type hologram, also called a "laser transmission" hologram. You don't have to cut it in half, just cut a hole in a piece of black paper and hold it over the hologram to show the image from random different positions on the hologram.

What is generally said about all parts of a hologram containing the whole image is false. A myth. In fact, each part of a hologram contains information about the image *from that particular range of perspective views*. A small piece has less information than a large piece. A single point on the hologram contains a single *perspective view*, and at much reduced resolution than is visible to the human eye looking at the original object from the same perspective.

posts.author: scienceinthegreen
posts.content_md:
Thanks BobH,

The MedCosm Computer Generated Hologram generates a transmission hologram. And yes I was wrong to imply that all the parts of a hologram contain all of the whole image. Because of this simplification/generalising (when I should know better) I hadn't thought of masking off regions - a far better idea than destructive cutting, and more likely to give a higher quality image. Thanks for that!

Now I need to source a (cheap) suitable laser - red led 5mW and preferably from a UK supplier. There are lots available - are they all as good each other?

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
If just need the hologram buy one of the teaching holograms from Integraf. If you want to make them then take a lens with you when you buy your laser and spread the beam onto a white card. If the beam is uniform and elliptical then it will make a hologram. (At least this has been my experience for lasers under 5mw.

If you just want the easy way to succeed get the kit from integraf with the laser.
